arxiv-2103-05520.title: Sustainability: Delivering Agility’s Promise
arxiv-2103-05520.creator: Jutta Eckstein, Claudia de O. Melo
arxiv-2103-05520.description: Abstract Sustainability is a promise by agile development, as it is part of both the Agile Alliance’s and the Scrum Alliance’s vision. Thus far, not much has been delivered on this promise. This paper explores the Agile Manifesto and points out how agility could contribute to sustainability in its three dimensions – social, economic, and environmental.

arxiv-2211-09001.title: Multi-Timescale Modeling of Human Behavior
arxiv-2211-09001.creator: Chinmai Basavaraj, Adarsh Pyarelal, Evan C Carter
arxiv-2211-09001.description: Abstract In recent years, the role of artificially intelligent (AI) agents has evolved from being basic tools to socially intelligent agents working alongside humans towards common goals. In such scenarios, the ability to predict future behavior by observing past actions of their human teammates is highly desirable in an AI agent.

arxiv-2212-09028.title: Neural Coreference Resolution based on Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2212-09028.creator: Yu Wang, Hongxia Jin
arxiv-2212-09028.description: Abstract The target of a coreference resolution system is to cluster all mentions that refer to the same entity in a given context. All coreference resolution systems need to solve two subtasks; one task is to detect all of the potential mentions, and the other is to learn the linking of an antecedent for each possible mention.

arxiv-2312-17206.title: Precision predictions for dark matter with DM@NLO in the MSSM Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-2312-17206.creator: Julia Harz e2,addr2, Björn Herrmann e1,addr1, Michael Klasen e3,addr3, Karol Kovařík e4,addr3, Luca Paolo Wiggering e5,addr3
arxiv-2312-17206.description: Abstract We present DM@NLO , a Fortran 77 based program with a C++ interface dedicated to precision calculations of dark matter (DM) (co)annihilation cross-sections and elastic dark matter-nucleon scattering amplitudes in the Minimal Supersymmetric (SUSY) Standard Model (MSSM) at next-to-leading order (NLO) in perturbative (SUSY) QCD.

arxiv-2401-16013.title: SERL: A Software Suite for Sample-Efficient Robotic Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2401-16013.creator: Jianlan Luo, Zheyuan Hu, Charles Xu, You Liang Tan, Jacob Berg, Archit Sharma, Stefan Schaal, Chelsea Finn, Abhishek Gupta, Sergey Levine
arxiv-2401-16013.description: Abstract In recent years, significant progress has been made in the field of robotic reinforcement learning (RL), enabling methods that handle complex image observations, train in the real world, and incorporate auxiliary data, such as demonstrations and prior experience. However, despite these advances, robotic RL remains hard to use.

arxiv-2402-15420.title: PREDILECT: Preferences Delineated with Zero-Shot Language-based Reasoning in Reinforcement Learning Conference: Proceedings of the 2024 ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction; March 11–14, 2024; Boulder, CO, USA Proceedings of the 2024 ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human
arxiv-2402-15420.creator: Simon Holk, Daniel Marta, Iolanda Leite
arxiv-2402-15420.description: Abstract . Preference-based reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a new field in robot learning, where humans play a pivotal role in shaping robot behavior by expressing preferences on different sequences of state-action pairs. However, formulating realistic policies for robots demands responses from humans to an extensive array of queries.

arxiv-2405-04814.title: A Novel Technique for Query Plan Representation Based on Graph Neural Nets
arxiv-2405-04814.creator: Baoming Chang, Amin Kamali, Verena Kantere
arxiv-2405-04814.description: Abstract Learning representations for query plans play a pivotal role in machine learning-based query optimizers of database management systems. To this end, particular model architectures are proposed in the literature to transform the tree-structured query plans into representations with formats learnable by downstream machine learning models.

arxiv-2406-02675.title: Graduate School of Informatics, Nagoya University, Nagoya 464-8601, Japan
arxiv-2406-02675.creator: max.washton@gmail.com
arxiv-2406-02675.description: Abstract On perturbation around closed exclusion processes Masataka Watanabe Abstract We derive the formula for the stationary states of particle-number conserving exclusion processes infinitesimally perturbed by inhomogeneous adsorption and desorption. The formula not only proves but also generalises the conjecture proposed in [Phys. Rev. E 97, 032135] to account for inhomogeneous adsorption and desorption.

arxiv-2601-01420.title: Alignment-Dependent Gapless Chiral Split Magnons in Altermagnetic Domain Walls
arxiv-2601-01420.creator: Zhaozhuo Zeng, Zhejunyu Jin, Peng Yan
arxiv-2601-01420.description: Abstract Altermagnets, an emerging class of magnetic materials, exhibit exotic chiral split magnons that are of great interest for both fundamental physics and spintronic applications. However, detecting and manipulating these magnons is challenging due to their THz frequency response. Here, we report the discovery of gapless chiral split magnons confined within altermagnetic domain walls.

pmc-10775111.title: Midterm outcomes of open repair versus endovascular descending thoracic aortic aneurysm repair
pmc-10775111.creator: Felix Orelaru, Katelyn Monaghan, Rana-Armaghan Ahmad, Kush Amin, Marc Titsworth, Jie Yang, Karen M Kim, Shinichi Fukuhara, Himanshu Patel, Bo Yang
pmc-10775111.description: ObjectiveThe study objective was to evaluate the midterm outcome of thoracic endovascular aortic repair compared with open repair in patients with descending thoracic aortic aneurysm.MethodsFrom August 1993 to February 2023, 499 patients with descending thoracic aortic aneurysms underwent open repair (n = 221) or thoracic endovascular aortic repair (n = 278).

pmc-11388266.title: Altered memory CCR6+ Th17-polarised T-cell function and biology in people with HIV under successful antiretroviral therapy and HIV elite controllers
pmc-11388266.creator: Alexis Yero, Jean-Philippe Goulet, Tao Shi, Cecilia T. Costiniuk, Jean-Pierre Routy, Cecile Tremblay, Ralph-Sydney Mboumba Bouassa, Yulia Alexandrova, Amélie Pagliuzza, Nicolas Chomont, Petronela Ancuta, Mohammad-Ali Jenabian
pmc-11388266.description: SummaryBackgroundDespite successful antiretroviral therapy (ART), frequencies and immunological functions of memory CCR6+ Th17-polarised CD4+ T-cells are not fully restored in people with HIV (PWH). Moreover, long-lived Th17 cells contribute to HIV persistence under ART. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these observations remain understudied.

pmc-11444779.title: Interactions between reptiles and people: a perspective from wildlife rehabilitation records
pmc-11444779.creator: Teagan Pyne, Ron Haering, Aditi Sriram, Shona Lorigan, Richard Shine, Chris J Jolly
pmc-11444779.description: As urbanization expands globally, human–wildlife interactions will inevitably increase. Here, we analysed 10 years of wildlife rehabilitation records of squamate (snake and lizard) reptiles (n = 37 075) from the Greater Sydney region, New South Wales, Australia, to explore their value to address management and conservation issues.

pmc-11535361.title: Case report: Novel approach to distal radius non-union treatment with free fibula flap reconstruction
pmc-11535361.creator: Maria Albuquerque, Luís Mata Ribeiro, Miguel Botton
pmc-11535361.description: IntroductionDistal radius fractures are common among adults. Despite being a rare complication, occurring in only 0.2 % of the cases, non-union poses significant treatment challenges.Presentation of caseIn this article, we report the case of a 43-year-old male with a history of distal radius fracture resulting from a motorcycle accident.

pmc-12505699.title: The dual burden of stigma: a scoping review of its impact on colorectal cancer patients and screening participants
pmc-12505699.creator: Wenjie Zhao, Mengmeng Chen, Jianyue Dai, Liwen Wang, Bin Li
pmc-12505699.description: BackgroundThe stigma caused by colorectal cancer (CRC) and CRC screening affects CRC prevention and treatment. Based on the Health Stigma and Discrimination Framework (HSDF), this review analyzed the influencing factors and mechanism of stigma in CRC.MethodsWe conducted a scoping review in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and CNKI.

pmc-12649478.title: Evolution of Anchor Polymer Systems Used in Arthroscopic Shoulder Surgery—A Comprehensive Review
pmc-12649478.creator: Eun-Ji Yoon, Kyeong-Eon Kwon, Jong-Ho Kim, Jian Li
pmc-12649478.description: Arthroscopic shoulder surgery has undergone significant evolution over the past decades, particularly in the materials used for suture anchors. The transition from metallic to bioabsorbable polymer anchors has revolutionized soft tissue-to-bone repair procedures, offering distinct advantages in terms of biocompatibility, imaging compatibility, and reduced complications.

pmc-12670096.title: Coagulation abnormalities in children with chronic liver disease and the association of these abnormalities with disease severity
pmc-12670096.creator: Rubaiyat Alam, Mst Arifa Main, Khan Lamia Nahid, Mohammad Rukunuzzaman
pmc-12670096.description: Background and aimsThis study aimed to evaluate the coagulation profile in children with chronic liver disease (CLD) and to investigate the relationship between coagulation abnormalities and disease severity.MethodsFifty-one consecutive children (mean age 7.4 ± 4.9 years) diagnosed with CLD were prospectively included and stratified by the Child–Pugh class (A, B, C).

pmc-13088531.title: Attitudes and knowledge of South African healthcare professionals towards blood flow restriction training
pmc-13088531.creator: Georgia Torres, Kameran Jacobsohn, Philippe Gradidge
pmc-13088531.description: ObjectiveBlood Flow Restriction Training (BFRT) has been shown to have similar benefits to high-intensity exercise conditions without high resistance loads. This training methodology is not included in traditional healthcare professional training, as it is an emerging training tool. Moreover, the attitudes and knowledge of healthcare professionals towards BFRT remain unknown in South Africa.

pmc-13091300.title: Demographic and socioeconomic inequalities in sleep quality among Chinese aged 15 years and above: a national population-based study
pmc-13091300.creator: Yingchen Sang, Zhiping Peng, Xinying Zeng, Ying Liu, Youjiao Wang, Xin Gao, Chi Zhang, Ding Zou, Zhili Huang, Fang Han, Shiwei Liu
pmc-13091300.description: SummaryBackgroundHigh-quality sleep is essential for health, yet sleep patterns and their prevalence within the Chinese population remain inadequately characterized. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of poor sleep quality and various sleep characteristics within China, and to explore the social gradients and inequalities in sleep quality to identify vulnerable populations.

pmc-13201853.title: Impact of a structured case report on self-reported responses to simulated emergency scenarios: a randomized survey-based study
pmc-13201853.creator: Christian Porschen, Katharina E M Hellenthal, Alexander Zarbock, Michael Fujarski, Paul Brauckmann, Thi Ngoc-Anh Nguyen, Sebastian Rehberg, Jan Wnent, Matthias Lange
pmc-13201853.description: Case reports are a long-standing component of medical research, but their association with self-reported responses to simulated clinical scenarios remains underexplored. This study investigated whether exposure to a structured case report influences simulated emergency medical decisions. This randomized survey-based study was conducted among licensed physicians between March and May 2025.
